thread:
alex: heads up — seeing a weird quality regression with the int4 bringup on RAG. long-context queries are returning concatenated fragments as facts and sometimes duplicating references. started after yesterday's quant kernel swap. :eyes:

maria: ugh. new after quant change or after the retriever ingest tweak?

alex: quant change first, retriever tweak later in the day. i repro by running the same query with a few long docs. looks like fragment boundaries get blurred when we concat+pad.

sam: i think this is the concat+padding collision we've talked about. if chunker uses a plain space join and the kernel remaps pad token id differently in int4 path, kvcache might mix tail tokens across fragments. minimal repro is trivial.

jin: can you paste a minimal repro here? we should create a micro-golden to isolate it.

alex: quick repro (staging):
```bash
# hit staging RAG endpoint with two overlapping fragments
curl -s -X POST https://staging-api.internal/redwood/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -d '{"model":"curie-q-int4","prompt":"<DOC1>...<DOC2>...\nquestion: who wrote the second doc?"}'
```
results: model returns combined author names and invents a third. not just hallucination — it's reusing tail tokens from doc1 in doc2 answer.

maria: we should add separators in chunker (explicit <SEP> token) and a small canonicalizer before fingerprinting. also add micro-golden examples that exercise adjacent-fragment attribution.

sam: agreed. i'll add a patch to chunker to use `\n<doc-sep>\n` plus a 2-byte non-letter delimiter, and update the padding mapper in quant runtime to preserve pad id mapping across kernels. will push to staging now.

ops-bot: deploy queued to staging: deploy-2026-06-14-axiom (sam/chunker-patch). ETA ~6m. :gear:

labeler-bot: new labeling batch LB-1214 created (80 items) — task: "adjacent-fragment attribution". priority: high. due: 48h. reviewers: @labeling-team.

maria: i'll add 20 micro-goldens to LB-1214 that specifically cover long-doc edgecases (code blocks, tables, bullets). also adding an eval suite entry: `rag-fragmentation-suite:v1`.

alex: nice. once staging deploy is up can someone run the eval harness and post qbench numbers? key metrics: hallucination rate on frag-suite, exact-match attribution, latency delta.

sam: running qbench after deploy. command i'm using:
```bash
python infra/qbench/run.py --suite rag-fragmentation-suite:v1 --model curie-q-int4 --output /tmp/qbench-int4.json
```
will post results in ~20m.

jin: i'm also gating the quant-kernel selector: if input context length > 1024 tokens, runtime falls back to fp16 for that request to avoid pad-id artifact until we finish end-to-end verification. no user-visible config change.

maria: good safety net. i'll notify labeling that LB-1214 needs manual checks for attribution (flag cases where answer cites wrong doc).

alex: assign @sam and @maria to own verification. tagging @labeling-team for LB-1214 pickup. thanks all. :thumbsup:

sam: qbench done — staging shows halluc rate down 78% on frag-suite, latency +6% p95. pushing full results to the eval dashboard now.

maria: great. i'll cherry-pick best micro-goldens into the global golden set after label review. then we can run canary on prod.

alex: plan: 1) labeling completes LB-1214, 2) cherry-pick goldens, 3) canary int4 with chunker-sep on 5% traffic. if no regressions in 24h we roll.

ops-bot: canary rollout scheduled: model curie-q-int4 -> 5% traffic in us-west on 2026-06-14T23:40Z.

jin: i'll monitor kernel fallback logs and add an alert if pad-id collisions spike.

alex: perfect. i'll open a follow-up ticket to refine chunking heuristics (overlap windows, normalization) so we reduce need for fallback.

maria: thanks — ping me if labeling needs more context or extra edgecases.

sam: will post final eval permalink shortly.

labeler-bot: LB-1214 status: 14/80 assigned, 0/80 completed. reminders sent.

alex: closing loop for now. will update when canary completes.
